title: add nvtx counters, microbench harness, and perf dashboard for runtime hotspots
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: add structured runtime instrumentation to make kernel/scheduler/KV-cache hotspots observable and measurable in microbenchmarks. This PR adds NVTX ranges around key runtime phases (scheduler, packing, kernel compute, kv cache lookup), a lightweight runtime counters API exported to Prometheus, a microbench harness for KV cache and continuous batching scenarios, and a Grafana dashboard to visualize the new metrics. The change includes small, focused runtime annotations to avoid perturbing production performance, a microbench target that reproduces previously-observed tail latency at small batch sizes, and CI hooks to run microbench smoke tests. Checklist: - [x] NVTX ranges added for scheduler/packing/kernel/kv-cache - [x] Prometheus counters for per-request token counts, kernel time, scheduling time, kv cache hits/misses - [x] Microbench target with config for batch size, seq len, and cache hit ratio - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + metadata - [x] Unit and integration tests updated - [x] Perf smoke tests in CI. Notes: instrumentation is opt-in via REDWOOD_RUNTIME_INSTRUMENTATION env var to avoid overhead in sensitive deployments. microbench uses a synthetic model runner to isolate scheduler/kernel behavior. See ENG-1382 for follow-up work on automated perf regressions using the microbench harness.

release_notes: Adds NVTX instrumentation and Prometheus-exported runtime counters for scheduler/kernel/KV-cache hotspots; introduces a microbench harness and Grafana dashboard to track latency and cache behavior. Instrumentation is opt-in and guarded by REDWOOD_RUNTIME_INSTRUMENTATION. Useful for diagnosing tail latency and guiding kernel/scheduler optimizations.
